evidence.title: No evidence, no claim.
evidence.lead: In Documents only mode, a sentence stays in the answer only while a passage supports it. Take the passage away and the claim goes with it.

evidence.refused: The provided documents do not answer this question.

evidence.note: Strict mode answers by meaning, so paraphrased and whole-document questions still work, but every fact has to come from your documents.

how.title: What happens to a page.
how.lead: From upload to cited answer, every step that touches your document runs on your machine.
how.s1d: PDF, Word, PowerPoint, images, text or code. The type, size and structure are checked before anything is read.
how.s1x: Signatures are checked, Office archives are inspected for zip bombs, and a duplicate is recognized by its content, not just its name.
how.s2d: Text layers are extracted directly. Scans and images are read with Persian and English OCR.
how.s2x: Persian PDF text is rebuilt in reading order from glyph positions, and OCR re-reads pages that are rotated, upside down or skewed.
how.s3d: Text is split into passages that remember their file and page, slide, paragraph or section.
how.s3x: Persian spelling is normalized, Word files are chunked under their headings, and a short bridge joins consecutive PDF pages.
how.s4d: Each passage gets a multilingual-e5 vector and joins a keyword index, both on your machine.
how.s4x: Keyword (BM25) and vector matches are fused, which helps with exact names, numbers and codes.
how.s5d: Passages live in Qdrant, filtered by the conversation they belong to. Delete it and they go too.
how.s5x: An indexed document can be reused in another conversation without uploading it again.
how.s6d: The closest passages go to the model with your question. The answer streams back with numbered citations.
how.s6x: Hybrid reranks candidates with a cross-encoder trained for Arabic script; Strict applies an evidence gate.
how.hint: Drag to turn it. Select a part to read about it.

privacy.title: You decide what leaves your machine.
privacy.lead: Reading, OCR, the search index and your conversations stay local. Only the model you choose decides where the answer is written.
privacy.localNote: Generation runs on this workstation. No prompt or excerpt leaves through the model adapter.
privacy.privateNote: Your question and the retrieved excerpts go to a server you control. Private OpenAI-compatible services can run without a key.
privacy.externalNote: Your question and the retrieved excerpts go to a third-party service. ParsRAG won't connect until you acknowledge this.
privacy.tableCaption: Compared with a typical cloud chatbot that reads files you upload to it.
privacy.always: API keys stay in memory or environment variables, never in browser storage, logs or API responses.

measured.title: Measured, then shipped.
measured.lead: Every number here links to where the repository records it. We'd rather show a small, honest gain than a big, vague claim.
measured.fusionD: Mean reciprocal rank on 127 keyword-style queries. Higher is better.
measured.fusionNote: 0.851 with the Hybrid reranker; on 125 paraphrased questions the change was within noise.
measured.rotD: Character error on Persian pages turned 90 degrees. Lower is better.
measured.rotNote: Pages skewed 5 degrees went from 0.40 to 0.24; upright pages were unchanged.
measured.ocrD: Mean character error after the 1.0 OCR changes. Lower is better.
measured.ocrNote: Grayscale at 200 dpi, no contrast stretching, a confidence-based second pass.
measured.e5T: A gain too small to turn on
measured.e5D: Vector-search MRR with E5 query and passage prefixes.
measured.e5Note: Too small to justify re-indexing everyone's documents, so it stays opt-in.
measured.gate1: An end-to-end test uploads a Persian PDF and requires a cited answer from the right page, and at least 7 of 8 paraphrased Persian questions must cite their own section first.
measured.gate2: Backend and frontend checks run on Linux, Windows and macOS.
measured.gate3: Backend test coverage may not drop below 85 percent.
measured.caveat: The retrieval and OCR figures were measured by the maintainer on document sets that aren't published, so they can't be reproduced from the public repository. The CI checks run in the open on every change.

formats.title: One shelf for what you read.
formats.lead: Office files, scans, data and code are read with their structure, so a citation can name a slide or a section, not just a file.
formats.label: File families
formats.b1x: Native structured extraction, with OCR for scanned or image-heavy PDF pages and for images inside Word and PowerPoint files.
formats.b2x: Validated, normalized and read with Persian and English OCR.
formats.b3x: UTF-8, UTF-16 or legacy Windows-1256 Persian and Windows-1252 text. JSON is validated and normalized.
formats.b4x: Visible text from markup, and plain text from configuration files.
formats.b5x: Extracted with section metadata, so answers can point into a file.
formats.limits: By default a conversation holds 10 files, each up to 100 MiB, with up to 500 MiB per upload. Office archives are checked for suspicious compression, and unsupported binaries are rejected rather than misread.

install.title: Run it on your machine.
install.lead: You need Docker Engine with Compose and 8–16 GB of RAM, depending on the model. After the first download, a local model works offline.
install.macGpu: Docker Desktop doesn't give containers access to a Mac's GPU. Use the CPU setup, run Ollama natively, or connect an API model.

cmt.start: Start Qdrant and Ollama, download the model, then start ParsRAG
cmt.apiEnv: In .env set LLM_PROVIDER=api, LLM_MODEL_NAME, MODEL_API_BASE_URL, MODEL_API_KEY and MODEL_API_DISCLOSURE_ACKNOWLEDGED=1

install.then: Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000. The first start downloads the embedding model and the reranker (about 100 MB) into the model cache.
